text:
**sqlpipe** streams PostgreSQL tables to S3 as Parquet files. Point it at a database, tell it which tables you want, and it handles the rest — batched reads, columnar conversion, and multipart uploads. No intermediate disk, no OOM on large tables.

It works as a single binary with no external dependencies beyond valid Postgres and S3 credentials. Run it on a cron, in a migration script, or as a one-off export. Schema inference is automatic; column types map to Parquet logical types so downstream tools (Athena, Spark, DuckDB) read them without extra configuration. Incremental syncs use a watermark column to avoid re-exporting unchanged rows.
